title: Causal Riverboard: Request Mapper & Correlation Heatline
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Purpose: Design a compact, high-density request drill-down workspace for the Redwood Console that surfaces causal relationships between spans across services, surface-level correlation fingerprints (Correlation IDs), and a timeline ‚heatline‘ that emphasizes request hotspots without overwhelming the primary request view. This ticket covers wireframes, an interactive Figma prototype, accessibility checks, and a small usability study with two internal engineering teams.

Scope:
- Top-level 'riverboard' canvas that shows request path as a horizontal progression with aggregated span microcards.
- Correlation Heatline: a compressed, color-graded bar beneath the timeline that encodes event density and KV cache hits/misses.
- Expandable span microcards that reveal span metadata, duration timeline, key tags, and quick links to logs and payload snapshots.
- Inline correlation fingerprint: hover to highlight all matching spans/requests that share correlation IDs, sampling ID, or custom trace tags.
- Filter composer exposed in the header with tokenized predicates (service:, span_type:, status:, correlation_id:), plus a lightweight quick-scope menu for time-range and lane (service/region) adjustments.
- Compact view for dense traces and an expanded view for step-by-step playback with scrubber and auto-play.

Design goals:
1) Reduce cognitive load when jumping from a dashboard-level alert to a starving request — user should find root-cause spans within 3 clicks.
2) Preserve signal-to-noise: make hotspots visually salient while keeping span metadata accessible in-place.
3) Enable ops to quickly copy correlation fingerprints and open a prepopulated Insights query.

Non-goals: deep callstack visualizer (handled by separate callgraph workstream), heavy flamegraphs, and full session replay (out of scope).
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype (interactive) implements riverboard canvas, heatline, microcard expansion, and tokenized filter composer
Prototype supports hover-to-highlight for correlation IDs across the visible timeline
Keyboard navigation and basic screenreader labels for microcards and filter tokens
Design review sign-off from Eng runtime and PM: comments addressed or captured as follow-ups
Usability test: median task completion time <= 2 minutes for 'locate the longest external call in request X' for 6/8 participants

Iterate to mid-fidelity and build Figma interactive prototype
Run a quick usability session (8 participants: 4 frontend, 4 runtime) and capture recordings
Address runtime feasibility notes (batching display, KV cache hit colors) with ENG
Prepare handoff artifact: design tokens, spacing, and microcard states for implementation

design_decisions: Use a horizontal river metaphor to make left-to-right time progression explicit; this reduces vertical scroll when viewing long traces
Encode density as a heatline beneath the main timeline to avoid overloading span microcards with visual noise
Prefer microcards with two-line summaries and an expand state for full metadata to balance scanability vs detail-on-demand
Tokenized filter composer instead of free text to encourage discoverability of common predicates and reduce parsing ambiguity

implementation_notes: Front-end: implement virtualized canvas with lane windowing to keep frame rate stable for traces > 2k spans
Back-end: provide aggregated span buckets per 100ms window and precomputed correlation_index to support heatline rendering
Telemetry: instrument 'copy correlation fingerprint' events and 'heatline zoom' interactions for future UX tuning
Feature-flag path: console.feature.riverboard = beta for 10% of accounts initially

usability_findings: Participants preferred the heatline when asked to find bursty activity — saved average 18s compared to baseline trace list
Correlation fingerprint copy action was used in 92% of lab tasks when locating cross-service errors
Two participants were confused by microcard expand affordance; changed chevron placement and added hover label
